subject: maths
title: Year 6 Prisms and Cross-Sections
seo_title: Year 6 Prisms and Cross-Sections Worksheets: Name Prisms, Compare Cross-Sections (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Compare the parallel cross-sections of objects and recognise their relationships to right prisms
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on prisms and cross-sections for the Australian Curriculum: name prisms by their cross-section, tell prisms from pyramids, cylinders and cones, compare cuts parallel to the base, and count faces, edges and vertices. 100 questions with an answer key, ready for Year 7.
key_big: A prism has the same cross-section all along its length, and it is named after that shape.
key_sub: Cut a prism parallel to its ends and you always get the same shape: a triangle for a triangular prism, a hexagon for a hexagonal prism. Pyramids and cones get smaller towards the point, so they are not prisms; a cylinder has a curved surface, so it is not a prism either.

faq.q: What do Year 6 students learn about prisms in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: In Year 6 (AC9M6SP01) students Compare the parallel cross-sections of objects and recognise that a right prism has the same cross-section all along its length, and is named after that shape.

faq.q: What is a cross-section of a prism?
faq.a: It is the flat face you get when you cut the prism parallel to its ends. For a prism it is always the same shape and size as the ends, for example a triangle for a triangular prism.
No. A cylinder has the same circle cross-section all the way along, but its ends are circles and it has a curved surface, while a prism has polygon ends and only flat faces.

faq.q: What is the difference between a prism and a pyramid?
faq.a: A prism has two matching ends joined by rectangles, so its cross-sections stay the same. A pyramid has one base and triangles that meet at a point, so its cross-sections get smaller towards the apex.

sets.title: Name the prism by its cross-section

items.q: What is the name of this prism?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. Each end has 8 sides, so it is an octagonal prism. 10 is its number of faces.

items.q: What shape is the cross-section of a triangular prism?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. A triangular prism has triangle ends, so every cross-section parallel to the ends is a triangle. The side faces are rectangles, but they do not give the prism its name.

items.q: What shape is the cross-section of a pentagonal prism?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. A pentagonal prism has pentagon ends, so every cross-section parallel to the ends is a pentagon. The side faces are rectangles, but they do not give the prism its name.

items.q: This object is a prism. What is its name?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. The ends are rectangles, so it is a rectangular prism. It has 6 faces, but “hexagonal” would mean the ends are hexagons.

items.q: This object is a prism. What is its name?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. The end looks like a house: a square with a triangle on top. Count its sides: 5. So it is a pentagonal prism, not a triangular prism.

items.q: This object is a prism. What is its name?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. This prism stands on one of its ends. The top and bottom are triangles, so it is a triangular prism.

items.q: A prism is named after the shape of its …
items.e: Every slice of a prism parallel to its ends is the same shape. That shape names the prism: triangle → triangular prism.

items.q: A prism has a cross-section that is a hexagon. What is its name?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. A hexagon cross-section gives a hexagonal prism.

items.q: Which object is a hexagonal prism?
items.e: A has two matching hexagon ends (6 sides) joined by rectangles. The others are a pentagonal prism, a hexagonal pyramid and an octagonal prism.

items.q: A prism has a cross-section with 7 sides (a heptagon). What is its name?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. 7 sides make a heptagon, so it is a heptagonal prism. 9 would be its number of faces.

items.q: A cube is a prism. What shape is its cross-section?
items.e: Any slice of a cube parallel to a face is a square. (Hexagon would come from its 6 faces, octagon from its 8 vertices.)

items.q: What is the name of this prism?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. The ends are right-angled triangles. They are still triangles, so it is a triangular prism.

items.q: In a right prism, what shape are the faces that join the two ends?
c: the same shape as the ends
items.e: In a right prism the ends are joined by rectangles. Triangles that meet at a point belong to a pyramid.

items.q: Name this prism.
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. Each end has 6 sides, so it is a hexagonal prism. 8 is its number of faces.

items.q: Name this prism.
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. The ends are squares and the long faces are rectangles, so it is a rectangular prism (also called a square prism). It is not a cube, because not all its faces are squares.

items.q: What shape is the cross-section of an octagonal prism?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. An octagonal prism has octagon ends, so every cross-section parallel to the ends is an octagon. The side faces are rectangles, but they do not give the prism its name.

items.q: Name this prism.
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. The two ends are triangles, so it is a triangular prism. Do not name it by its 5 faces: that would give “pentagonal”.

items.q: Name this prism.
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. The top and bottom are matching hexagons joined by rectangles, so it is a hexagonal prism.

items.q: Which object is a triangular prism?
items.e: D has two matching triangle ends joined by rectangles. The pyramids have triangles that meet at a point.

items.q: What is the name of this prism?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. Count the sides of an end: 5 sides, so it is a pentagonal prism. 7 is its number of faces.

items.q: Is this object a prism?
c: Yes, it is a prism with a square cross-section
Yes, it is a hexagonal prism
No, a cube is not a prism
items.e: A cube has two matching square ends joined by squares (special rectangles). Every slice parallel to a face is the same square, so a cube is a prism.

items.q: Which object has the same cross-section all along its length but is NOT a prism?
items.e: Every slice of a cylinder is the same circle, but it is not a prism because it has a curved surface and circle ends. A cube is a prism.

items.q: Is this object a prism?
c: Yes, it is a triangular prism
Yes, it is a rectangular prism
No, it is a triangular pyramid
items.e: All 4 faces are triangles and 3 of them meet at a point. A triangular prism has 2 triangles joined by 3 rectangles.

items.q: Which object is NOT a prism?
items.e: B is a hexagonal pyramid: its triangles meet at a point. The others are a triangular prism, a cube and a hexagonal prism.

items.q: Which object is a prism?
items.e: A pentagonal prism has two matching pentagon ends joined by 5 rectangles. A cylinder has a curved surface, so it is not a prism.

items.q: Which is true about every pyramid?
c: It has one base and triangles that meet at a point
Its cross-sections are all the same size
Its base is always a square
items.e: A pyramid has one base (any polygon) and triangle faces that meet at the apex. Its base can be a triangle, square, pentagon and so on.

c: Yes, it is a triangular prism
Yes, it is a circular prism
items.e: A cone has 1 circle base and a curved surface that comes to a point. It only looks like a triangle from the side.

items.q: Which is true about every prism?
c: It has two matching, parallel ends joined by rectangles
It has one base and triangles that meet at a point
items.e: That is what makes a right prism. One base with triangles meeting at a point describes a pyramid.

c: No, its ends are circles and it has a curved surface
Yes, it is a rectangular prism
Yes, it is a circular prism
items.e: Every slice of a cylinder parallel to its ends is the same circle, but a prism has only flat faces and its ends are polygons. So a cylinder is not a prism.

items.q: Lachlan says, “This object has triangle faces, so it is a triangular prism.” The object has 1 square face and 4 triangle faces. Is he right?
c: No, it is a square-based pyramid
No, it is a rectangular prism
Yes, it is a triangular prism
items.e: 4 triangles that meet at a point on a square base make a square-based pyramid. A triangular prism has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles.

items.q: Why is a square-based pyramid not a prism?
c: Its cross-sections get smaller towards the top
items.e: A prism has the same cross-section all the way along. A pyramid’s slices shrink to a point. A triangular prism also has triangle faces and 5 faces, so those are not the reason.

items.q: Which object is NOT a prism?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point. The others have two matching ends joined by rectangles.
C has two matching pentagon ends joined by rectangles, so it is a pentagonal prism. The pyramid and the cone come to a point, and the cylinder has a curved surface.

items.q: How many of these objects are prisms? cube, cone, triangular prism, cylinder, square-based pyramid, hexagonal prism
items.e: The prisms are the cube, the triangular prism and the hexagonal prism: 3. The cone and the pyramid get smaller to a point, and the cylinder has a curved surface.

items.q: Why is a cylinder not a prism?
c: Its ends are circles and it has a curved surface
items.e: A cylinder keeps the same circle all the way along, but a prism must have polygon ends and only flat faces. A cylinder has 2 flat circle faces and 1 curved surface.

items.q: Is this object a prism?
c: No, it has a triangle on top
Yes, it is a triangular prism
Yes, it is a pentagonal prism
items.e: Its two ends are matching pentagons (a square with a triangle on top has 5 sides), joined by rectangles. So it is a pentagonal prism.

c: No, it has no flat faces
Yes, every slice is a circle
Yes, it is a circular prism
items.e: A sphere has one curved surface and no flat faces. Its slices are circles of different sizes, so it is not a prism.

items.q: Is this object a prism?
c: No, it is a square-based pyramid
Yes, it is a square prism
Yes, it is a triangular prism
items.e: It has 1 square base and 4 triangles that meet at a point. Its cross-sections get smaller towards the top, so it is a pyramid, not a prism.

items.q: Is this object a prism?
c: No, it is a hexagonal pyramid
Yes, it is a hexagonal prism
Yes, it is a heptagonal prism
items.e: It has 1 hexagon base and 6 triangles that meet at a point, so it is a hexagonal pyramid. (7 faces does not make it heptagonal.)

items.q: Is this object a prism?
c: Yes, it is an octagonal prism
No, it is a hexagonal pyramid
Yes, it is a hexagonal prism
items.e: It has two matching hexagons joined by rectangles. A prism is still a prism when it stands on its end.

items.q: This object is cut parallel to its base. The red face shows the cut. What is the cross-section?
c: a square, smaller than the base
a square the same size as the base
items.e: A cut parallel to the base of a square-based pyramid is a square. The cut is nearer the apex, so the square is smaller than the base. The triangles are the side faces, not the cross-section.

items.q: This object is cut parallel to its base. The red face shows the cut. What shape is the cross-section?
items.e: The object is a rectangular prism. Every cut parallel to its base is the same shape as the base: a rectangle.

items.q: This object is cut parallel to its base. The red face shows the cut. What is the cross-section?
c: a triangle the same size as the base
a triangle, smaller than the base
items.e: The base is a triangle, so a cut parallel to the base is also a triangle. In a pyramid it gets smaller the closer you cut to the apex.

items.q: This object is cut parallel to its base. The red face shows the cut. What shape is the cross-section?
items.e: The object is a hexagonal prism. Every cut parallel to its base is the same shape as the base: a hexagon.

c: a circle, smaller than the base
a circle the same size as the base
items.e: A cut parallel to the base of a cone is a circle. It is smaller than the base because the cone narrows to a point. A triangle comes from cutting straight down through the point, not parallel to the base.
A is a cube, a prism, so every cut parallel to the base is the same square. The cone and the pyramids get smaller towards the point, so their cuts are smaller than the base.

items.q: This object is cut parallel to its base. The red face shows the cut. What shape is the cross-section?
items.e: The object is a triangular prism. Every cut parallel to its base is the same shape as the base: a triangle.

items.q: A long chocolate box has two triangle ends joined by 3 rectangles. Liam cuts the box parallel to an end. What shape is the cut?
items.e: The box is a triangular prism. Cuts parallel to its ends are triangles, the same as the ends.

items.q: When you cut a prism parallel to its ends, every cross-section is …
c: the same shape and size as the ends
items.e: That is what makes a prism: it has the same cross-section all along its length.

items.q: Isla cuts a cone parallel to its base and says the cut face is a triangle. What did she mix up?
c: The cut face is a rectangle
The cut face is a square
A cut straight down through the point gives a triangle; a cut parallel to the base gives a circle
Nothing: the cut face is a triangle
items.e: A cone looks like a triangle from the side, but a cut parallel to its base is always a circle.

items.q: This object is cut parallel to its base. The red face shows the cut. What shape is the cross-section?
items.e: The object is a pentagonal prism. Every cut parallel to its base is the same shape as the base: a pentagon.

items.q: Which object has every cross-section parallel to its base the same shape and size?
items.e: A prism has the same cross-section all the way along. Pyramids and cones get smaller towards the point, and a sphere’s circles change size.

items.q: Cuts parallel to the base of an object are squares that get smaller and smaller until they reach a point. What is the object?
items.e: Squares that shrink to a point make a square-based pyramid. If the squares stayed the same size it would be a prism.

items.q: Mei saws an unsharpened pencil (a hexagonal prism) in half, straight across, parallel to its end. What shape is the outline of the cut face?
items.e: The pencil is a hexagonal prism, so a cut parallel to the end is a hexagon. (The lead in the middle is a small circle, but the outline of the cut is a hexagon.)

items.q: A prism is cut parallel to its ends. The cross-section is a pentagon. How many faces does the prism have?
items.e: It is a pentagonal prism: 2 pentagon ends + 5 rectangles = 7 faces. 6 would be a pentagonal pyramid.

items.q: Every cut parallel to the base of an object is a circle of the same size. What is the object?
items.e: A cylinder has the same circle all the way along. A cone’s circles get smaller, and a sphere’s circles grow and then shrink.

items.q: When you cut a pyramid parallel to its base, the cross-sections …
c: are all the same size as the base
are the same shape as the base but get smaller towards the apex
items.e: Each slice is a smaller copy of the base. At the apex it shrinks to a point.

items.q: A loaf of sandwich bread is shaped like a rectangular prism with square ends. Mia cuts it into slices parallel to the ends. What shape is each slice?
c: a rectangle as long as the loaf
a square, the same size as the ends
items.e: Cuts parallel to the ends of a prism are the same as the ends: every slice is the same square.

c: a circle the same size as the ends
items.e: Every cut of a cylinder parallel to its ends is the same circle. It looks like an oval only because we see it at an angle.

items.q: Every cut parallel to the base of an object is the same hexagon. What is the object?
items.e: The same hexagon all the way along means a hexagonal prism. In a hexagonal pyramid the hexagons get smaller.

sets.title: Faces, edges and vertices of prisms

items.q: A prism has 10 vertices. What is its name?
items.e: Half the vertices are on each end: 10 ÷ 2 = 5, so the ends are pentagons.

items.q: How many edges does a pentagonal prism have?
items.e: A pentagonal prism has 7 faces (2 pentagons + 5 rectangles), 15 edges (5 + 5 + 5) and 10 vertices (5 + 5). Do not forget the 5 edges that join the two ends.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles + 3 rectangles), 9 edges (3 + 3 + 3) and 6 vertices (3 + 3). You can see only 3 faces, but the bottom and the back end count too.

items.q: Which has more edges, a pentagonal prism or a pentagonal pyramid, and by how many?
items.e: Prism: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15 edges. Pyramid: 5 round the base + 5 up to the apex = 10. 15 − 10 = 5.

items.q: This is a rectangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces (2 rectangles + 4 rectangles), 12 edges (4 + 4 + 4) and 8 vertices (4 + 4). Dashed lines show edges at the back that you cannot see.

items.q: This is a pentagonal prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A pentagonal prism has 7 faces (2 pentagons + 5 rectangles), 15 edges (5 + 5 + 5) and 10 vertices (5 + 5). Dashed lines show edges at the back that you cannot see.

items.q: This is a hexagonal prism. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A hexagonal prism has 8 faces (2 hexagons + 6 rectangles), 18 edges (6 + 6 + 6) and 12 vertices (6 + 6).

items.q: How many more vertices does a hexagonal prism have than a hexagonal pyramid?
items.e: Prism: 6 + 6 = 12 vertices. Pyramid: 6 on the base + 1 apex = 7. 12 − 7 = 5.

items.q: A triangular prism and a square-based pyramid both have 5 faces. How else are they different?
c: The prism has 5 vertices and the pyramid has 6
The prism has 6 vertices and the pyramid has 5
They have the same number of edges
items.e: Triangular prism: 9 edges, 6 vertices. Square-based pyramid: 8 edges, 5 vertices.

items.q: How many edges does a hexagonal prism have?
items.e: A hexagonal prism has 8 faces (2 hexagons + 6 rectangles), 18 edges (6 + 6 + 6) and 12 vertices (6 + 6). Edges round both ends (6 + 6) plus 6 joining them.

items.q: This is a hexagonal prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A hexagonal prism has 8 faces (2 hexagons + 6 rectangles), 18 edges (6 + 6 + 6) and 12 vertices (6 + 6). Do not forget the 2 hexagon ends.

items.q: How many vertices does a heptagonal prism have?
items.e: A heptagonal prism has 9 faces (2 heptagons + 7 rectangles), 21 edges (7 + 7 + 7) and 14 vertices (7 + 7).

items.q: A prism’s cross-section has n sides. Which rule gives its number of faces?
items.e: There are n rectangles plus the 2 ends: n + 2. (n + 1 is the rule for a pyramid, 2 × n gives the vertices and 3 × n gives the edges.)

items.q: A prism has 8 faces. What shape is its cross-section?
items.e: Faces = 2 ends + the number of sides. 8 − 2 = 6 sides, so the ends are hexagons. (Heptagon uses the pyramid rule: 8 − 1.)

items.q: How many faces does an octagonal prism have?
items.e: An octagonal prism has 10 faces (2 octagons + 8 rectangles), 24 edges (8 + 8 + 8) and 16 vertices (8 + 8).

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles + 3 rectangles), 9 edges (3 + 3 + 3) and 6 vertices (3 + 3). 3 edges round each end and 3 joining the ends.

items.q: How many vertices does a triangular prism have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles + 3 rectangles), 9 edges (3 + 3 + 3) and 6 vertices (3 + 3).

items.q: A prism has 18 edges. What shape is its cross-section?
items.e: A prism has 3 edges for every side of its end (round the front, round the back, and joining them). 18 ÷ 3 = 6, so the ends are hexagons.

items.q: How many edges does an octagonal prism have?
items.e: An octagonal prism has 10 faces (2 octagons + 8 rectangles), 24 edges (8 + 8 + 8) and 16 vertices (8 + 8).

items.q: This is a pentagonal prism. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A pentagonal prism has 7 faces (2 pentagons + 5 rectangles), 15 edges (5 + 5 + 5) and 10 vertices (5 + 5).

sets.title: Prisms in real life: tents, pencils, boxes and more

items.q: Grace makes the frame of a hexagonal prism from straws, one straw for each edge. How many straws does she need?
items.e: Edges: 6 round each end + 6 joining them = 18. 12 is the number of vertices and 8 the number of faces.

items.q: A chocolate box is a triangular prism. Each triangle end has sides of 4 cm, and the box is 20 cm long. Oliver runs ribbon along every edge. How much ribbon is that?
items.e: Edges round the two ends: 6 × 4 = 24 cm. Three long edges: 3 × 20 = 60 cm. Total: 24 + 60 = 84 cm.

items.q: Chloe slices a carrot from the thick end to the thin end. The slices are circles that get smaller. Which object is the carrot most like?
items.e: Circles that get smaller towards a point match a cone. A cylinder would give circles that are all the same size.

items.q: Charlotte stacks square tiles, each one smaller than the one below, with their centres in a line. Which object is the stack most like?
items.e: The square cross-sections get smaller towards the top, like a square-based pyramid. In a prism they would all be the same size.

items.q: Sienna makes the frames of a pentagonal prism and a pentagonal pyramid from straws, one straw for each edge. How many straws altogether?
items.e: Prism: 15 edges. Pyramid: 5 round the base + 5 up to the apex = 10. 15 + 10 = 25. (30 counts the prism twice; 16 adds the vertices, 10 + 6.)

items.q: At the swimming carnival, the pool is deeper at one end. From the side, the water is a trapezium, and it is the same all the way across the pool. What object is the water shaped like?
c: a prism with a trapezium cross-section
items.e: The water has the same trapezium cross-section from one side of the pool to the other, so it is a prism with trapezium ends.

items.q: Amelia stacks 10 identical hexagon tiles exactly on top of each other. What object does the stack look like?
items.e: Every layer is the same hexagon, so the stack has the same cross-section all the way up: a hexagonal prism.

items.q: At the sausage sizzle, every slice of a long round salami is the same circle. Is the salami shaped like a prism?
c: No, it is shaped like a cylinder
No, it is shaped like a cone
items.e: The same circle all along is a cylinder. It has a curved surface, so it is not a prism.

items.q: Harper cuts a party hat (a cone) parallel to its rim, partway up. What shape is the cut?
c: a circle the same size as the rim
a circle, smaller than the rim
items.e: A cut parallel to the base of a cone is a circle. It is smaller than the rim because the cone narrows to a point.

items.q: Ava’s family tent has two triangle ends, two sloping sides and a floor. What object is the tent shaped like?
items.e: Two triangle ends joined by rectangles (2 sides and the floor) make a triangular prism. Do not use the 5 faces to name it.

items.q: A block of cheese has two triangle ends joined by rectangles. Zara cuts it parallel to a triangle end. What shape is the cut face?
items.e: The cheese is a triangular prism, so every cut parallel to the ends is the same triangle.

items.q: William sands every face of a wooden block shaped like an octagonal prism. How many faces does he sand?
items.e: 2 octagon ends + 8 rectangles = 10 faces. 9 would be an octagonal pyramid and 16 is the number of vertices.

items.q: Ethan uses balls of modelling clay to join straws at the corners of a pentagonal prism. How many balls of clay does he need?
items.e: One ball for each vertex: 5 on each pentagon end, 5 + 5 = 10. 15 is the number of edges.

items.q: A chocolate bar comes in a long box with two triangle ends. Jack flattens the box for recycling. How many faces of cardboard are there?
items.e: The box is a triangular prism: 2 triangles + 3 rectangles = 5 faces. 9 is the number of edges.

items.q: Leo’s birdhouse has a front and a back shaped like a house (a square with a triangle roof), joined by rectangles. What object is it?
items.e: The house shape has 5 sides, so the birdhouse is a pentagonal prism.

items.q: Matilda tapes every edge of a cube-shaped gift box. Each edge is 20 cm long. How much tape does she use?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges: 12 × 20 = 240 cm. 120 cm uses the 6 faces, 160 cm the 8 vertices and 80 cm only 4 edges.

items.q: Cooper says the Great Pyramid of Giza is a prism. Why is he wrong?
c: Its cross-sections get smaller towards the top
It is too big to be a prism
items.e: The Great Pyramid is a square-based pyramid: its square slices shrink to a point. A prism keeps the same cross-section all the way up.

items.q: Noah paints each face of a wooden triangular prism a different colour. How many colours does he use?
items.e: A triangular prism has 2 triangles + 3 rectangles = 5 faces.

items.q: Aarav cuts a wooden beam with a square end into 4 shorter pieces, with cuts parallel to the end. What is each piece?
c: a prism with a square cross-section
items.e: Cuts parallel to the end keep the same square cross-section, so each piece is still a prism (a rectangular prism with square ends). It is only a cube if the piece is exactly as long as the square is wide.

items.q: Kai’s pencil is a hexagonal prism. How many long flat faces run down its side (not counting the ends)?
items.e: A hexagon has 6 sides, so there are 6 rectangles along the pencil. 8 counts the 2 ends as well, and 3 is how many you can see at once.
